title: Seminar on Economic Choices: Comparing Sources with Limitations
instructions: 阅读一篇关于经济选择研讨会的文章，注意不同来源的局限性。完成10道阅读理解题（单选、填空、匹配、判断正误/未提及）。然后学习语法：复合句与简单句搭配，条件、让步和原因表达，标点。完成8道语法题。最后进行口语和写作练习。所有材料为模拟教学用途，非官方雅思测试。
passage:
Last Friday, the Economics Society at Northbridge University held a seminar titled 'Comparing Economic Choices.' The event was designed to help students evaluate sources that have different limitations. Dr. Chen, the main speaker, began by saying, 'Every source has a limitation. Your job is to find it.'

A. The first source was a government report from 2022. It stated that the average household saved 12% of its income. However, the report only included families with two parents and two children. Dr. Chen noted, 'This sample is narrow, so the 12% figure may not apply to single-parent families or larger households.' Students wrote this limitation in their notes.

B. The second source was a newspaper article about a local market. The article claimed that vegetable prices had risen by 30% in one month. But the article did not mention that the survey covered only one small market in the city. 'A single market cannot represent the whole city,' Dr. Chen explained. 'The price increase might be real, but the scope is limited.'

C. The third source was a blog post by a consumer group. It argued that people should buy locally produced food to support the economy. The blog gave examples of successful local farms. However, it did not provide data on whether buying local actually increased overall economic benefit. Dr. Chen said, 'The argument is persuasive, but it lacks evidence. You need numbers, not just stories.'

After comparing the three sources, Dr. Chen asked the students to work in pairs. Each pair had to choose one source and explain its main limitation. Maria and Tom chose the government report. Maria said, 'The report's sample is too specific. It only looks at one type of family.' Tom agreed, but added, 'Still, the report is official, so its data might be more reliable than the blog's stories.' Dr. Chen overheard this and said, 'Good point, Tom. Reliability and limitation are different things. A source can be reliable but still limited.'

The seminar ended with a group discussion. Dr. Chen asked, 'If you were writing a report on household savings, which source would you use?' Several students raised their hands. One student, Aisha, said, 'I would use the government report, but I would also look for data on other family types.' Dr. Chen nodded. 'That's the right approach. Always ask: What does this source leave out?'

The seminar lasted two hours. At the end, students filled out a feedback form. Most students said they found the comparison exercise useful. Dr. Chen reminded them, 'When you read any economic claim, check the sample, the scope, and the evidence. If one is missing, the claim is weaker.'

grammar.title: 复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点
grammar.explanation: 在英语写作中，复合句（包含两个或以上主谓结构）和简单句（只有一个主谓结构）可以搭配使用，使文章有节奏。条件句常用 if 引导，表示'如果'；让步句常用 although/though/even though 引导，表示'虽然'；原因句常用 because/since/as 引导，表示'因为'。注意标点：当从句在前时，后面用逗号；当主句在前时，从句前不用逗号。例如：'If you were writing a report, which source would you use?'（条件句，从句在前，用逗号）；'The argument is persuasive, but it lacks evidence.'（简单句用 but 连接，逗号分隔）。
grammar.example: If you were writing a report on household savings, which source would you use?
